title: af/evaluate-input@2 Worker input
description: The exact, role-scoped input the independent evaluator receives for one implement Task (ADR-0028, ADR-0046). It is Worker Input, not a log record: no Task event references it, but it is durable in the CAS and named by `af/worker-evidence@1`'s context manifest, which is what makes the manifest's claim about what the evaluator was shown checkable. `@2` replaces `@1`'s complete mutation path lists with a bounded summary; the change was breaking because `mutations.added` went from an array of paths to an integer count.

goal.description: The operator's verbatim goal. The evaluator judges the derived Snapshot against this and nothing else.

derived_snapshot_id.description: The Snapshot materialized read-only as the evaluator's sandbox: the tree the verdict is about.

mutations.description: The bounded summary of what the implementer changed. `count`/`added`/`modified`/`deleted` are exact totals; `sample` is at most 20 paths and `truncated` says whether it is partial. `artifact` names the `af/derived-snapshot@1` record holding the complete lists — durable once, and not fetchable from the evaluator's sandbox.

sample.description: Sorted across all three kinds, capped at `MUTATION_SAMPLE` (20). Illustrative, never the scope signal — the counts are.

gates.description: Every acceptance Gate the kernel ran on the derived Snapshot, in pipeline order. All of them passed, or the Task would not have reached the evaluator.

output_contract.description: The exact shape of the one JSON object the evaluator must return, restated in the input so the Worker never has to infer it.

budget.description: The bounded reservation for this Attempt (ADR-0028). `reserved_tokens` is what the kernel charged the run budget before dispatch, not a quota the Worker must spend.
